title: Johnny Depp Is Scrooge: 'Ebenezer' Takes Over London as the Comeback Hits Theaters Friday
excerpt: Johnny Depp walked the Leicester Square red carpet Monday for the global premiere of 'Ebenezer,' Ti West's dark take on 'A Christmas Carol,' opening in theaters Nov. 13.
content:
London got Scrooged on Monday night. Johnny Depp took over Leicester Square for the global premiere of Ebenezer, Paramount's new take on Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol, stepping onto the red carpet as Ebenezer Scrooge himself — a role the studio describes as "deliciously unpleasant."

The premiere, held November 9 at the Odeon Luxe Leicester Square, brought out director Ti West, producer Emma Watts and screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern, along with co-stars Rupert Grint, Tramell Tillman, Sam Claflin, Ellie Bamber, Henry Lloyd-Hughes and Charlie Murphy. The red carpet was dressed for the season, with Christmas trees, artificial snow and 1950s festive songs playing as the cast arrived.

West is best known for the horror hits X, Pearl and MaXXXine, and his version of Dickens is billed as a "thrilling reimagining of the most iconic ghost story of all time." It is rated PG-13 for frightening material — a warning that fits a film about a man visited by three ghosts in a single night. The ensemble also includes Andrea Riseborough, Daisy Ridley, Arthur Conti and Ian McKellen.

Ebenezer opens in theaters on Friday, November 13, in the United States and the United Kingdom, including Dolby Cinema, 4DX and D-BOX screens. The film is being widely described as Depp's comeback, his first major leading role since the legal battles that kept him out of Hollywood studio films. Reports that a strong showing could revive talk of a Pirates of the Caribbean return remain unconfirmed.

Analysis: A ghost story with a second act built in

The timing is no accident. A dark, wintry Dickens adaptation landing the Friday before the holiday season gives Paramount a film that can play as both a prestige event and a crowd-pleaser, and Depp's name on the marquee is the story within the story. Whether audiences embrace a horror director's Scrooge will be decided at the box office this weekend — but Monday night in Leicester Square, the comeback narrative was already written, and Depp looked ready to own it.
